statement: Each citation was checked against PubMed on the date shown. No source has been read in full. Listing a source here does not mean any statement in the course is supported by it: support is recorded claim by claim, with a locator, in the claim register. Textbook chapters named in the original plan are not listed because they were not available to the build.

sources.authors: Feller-Kopman DJ, Reddy CB, DeCamp MM, et al.
sources.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
sources.limits: Concerns malignant pleural effusion. Its recommendations are described in the abstract as weak recommendations. Abstract read; full text not read.

sources.title: WABIP/AABIP statement on therapeutic indications of medical thoracoscopy for benign pleural disease
sources.authors: Chaddha U, Agrawal A, Ghori U, et al.
sources.limits: Concerns benign pleural disease only. Its abstract presents it as a consensus statement rather than a formal clinical practice guideline. Abstract read; full text not read.

sources.title: Effect of Thoracoscopic Talc Poudrage vs Talc Slurry via Chest Tube on Pleurodesis Failure Rate Among Patients With Malignant Pleural Effusions: A Randomized Clinical Trial
sources.authors: Bhatnagar R, Piotrowska HEG, Laskawiec-Szkonter M, et al.
sources.limits: Patients with confirmed malignant effusion who could undergo thoracoscopy under local anaesthesia. It excluded patients who needed thoracoscopy for diagnosis or had evidence of nonexpandable lung. No significant difference in pleurodesis failure at 90 days, and the abstract notes the study may have been underpowered. Abstract read; full text not read.

sources.title: Medical thoracoscopy with talc poudrage and indwelling pleural catheter insertion versus medical thoracoscopy with talc poudrage alone for patients with symptomatic malignant pleural effusion (TACTIC): a randomised, controlled phase 3 trial
sources.authors: Dipper A, Sundaralingam A, Hedley E, et al.
sources.limits: Patients with symptomatic malignant effusion in 11 UK hospitals. The co-primary outcomes, time in hospital and breathlessness, did not differ significantly; a result that is not significant is not evidence of equivalence. Fewer further invasive pleural procedures was a separate result. Abstract read; full text not read.

sources.title: Medical Thoracoscopy With vs Without Prior Artificial Pneumothorax for Patients With Minimal or Absent Pleural Effusion
sources.authors: Wang K, Zhou L, Zhu M, et al.
sources.limits: Patients with minimal or absent pleural effusion. The primary outcome was pleural access success, tested for noninferiority. It is not a general rule about entry. Abstract read; full text not read.
